title: When Something Goes Wrong
drDigitalIntro:
Computers act up sometimes — and that is completely normal. Here is how to stay calm and fix it.
• If an app freezes (stops responding), do not keep clicking — that makes things worse. The spinning indicator means the computer is struggling.
• Force-quit the frozen app: click the system menu and choose Force Quit. This closes the stuck app without affecting the rest of your computer.
• Reopen it fresh from the dock. Most freezes are temporary — the app starts normally again.
• Once the app is back, test that it really works by typing or clicking inside it before moving on.
• If force-quitting does not help, the next step is a full restart (covered in the next lesson).

playgroundTask.goal: You fixed a frozen app and confirmed it is working
playgroundTask.scenario: Notes is frozen and not responding

steps.say: Notes is frozen — it shows 'Not Responding.' Try clicking on it to see what happens.
Nothing happened — the app is stuck. Click the system menu (three dots) in the menu bar to open Force Quit.
Notes shows 'Not Responding.' Click Force Quit to close it.
Notes is closed. Click Notes in the dock to reopen it fresh.
Notes is back! Type something in it to confirm it is working.

drDigitalSuccess: You fixed the frozen app and confirmed it works! Force Quit + reopen solves most temporary freezes.
drDigitalHint: Click the frozen window, then use the system menu to Force Quit, reopen from the dock, and type something in Notes.
